lines.text: This man survived sixty hours inside a sunken ship.
Nigeria, May 2013. The tug Jascon-4 capsized.
The cook, Harrison Okene, was in the toilet.
It settled on the seabed, about thirty metres down.
In the dark, he found a pocket of air.
About four feet high.
Every breath made that air more toxic.
Eleven crewmates never made it out.
On day three, divers arrived.
Not to rescue anyone. To recover bodies.
On the camera feed, a hand appeared.
Everyone assumed it was another body.
Then the hand grabbed him.
Okene was alive. But he couldn't just swim up.
Days at depth had saturated his body with gas.
A fast ascent could have killed him.
They brought him up into a decompression chamber.
One expert estimated the air turned dangerous around hour fifty-six.
He was found near hour sixty.
They came for the dead and found him breathing.
